how_to_use_this_file: This file is a decision constraint, not a mood board. Every rule here is traceable to something the recruiter is trying to do or afraid of getting wrong.

It deliberately does not name a reference company. Borrowing another product's surface imports decisions made for a different user with a different job. Borrow the reasoning instead: identify the specific anxiety this user walks in with, and remove it.
If a proposed change cannot be justified against one of the principles below, it is decoration and does not ship.

the_user_and_the_job.who: An in-house recruiter screening hundreds of applicants per role, in daylight, alongside an ATS tab and a PDF resume.
the_user_and_the_job.job_to_be_done: Get from a pile of applicants to a shortlist I can defend to a hiring manager, without missing someone good.
dominant_emotions: fear of being wrong about a person
the_user_and_the_job.design_test: Every decision must reduce overwhelm or reduce fear of being wrong. Decisions that do neither are cost.

design_principles.name: Never show a number you cannot explain
design_principles.why: An opaque score in a high-stakes judgement transfers risk to the user without giving them control. They either over-trust it or ignore it — both are failures.
design_principles.in_practice: Every match score is a button onto its own reasoning: sub-scores, the weight each carried, and the underlying fact (which skills are missing, years against the bar). Scores are always attributed to the role they were computed against.

design_principles.name: Colour means state, not brand
design_principles.why: Colour is the scarcest attention resource in a dense decision tool. Spending it on identity leaves nothing to spend on meaning.
design_principles.in_practice: One accent for the single action we want taken on a screen; a semantic scale (pass / needs a look / fails) for candidate state. Everything else is greyscale. Brand identity lives in typography and layout, not in hue.

design_principles.name: Undo over confirm
design_principles.why: The real work is confidently eliminating most applicants. A confirm dialog taxes every action to guard against the rare wrong one; undo makes the common action free and the rare mistake cheap.
design_principles.in_practice: Destructive and bulk actions apply immediately and surface a persistent, specific undo affordance ('12 moved to Rejected — Undo'). No modal confirmations for stage changes.

design_principles.name: Show uncertainty rather than fake confidence
design_principles.why: Extraction and scoring are heuristics. Presenting a guess in the same visual language as a fact is the product quietly lying, and it is discovered exactly when trust matters most.
design_principles.in_practice: Low-confidence extractions look different from confirmed ones and invite correction. Missing data scores neutral, never best, and says so in words. Corrections visibly move the counts they affect.

design_principles.name: Density with escape hatches
design_principles.why: Volume work needs many rows on screen; judgement needs depth on one person. Forcing a choice between them costs the user either context or navigation.
design_principles.in_practice: Dense default tables, with detail expanded in place rather than reached by navigating away and losing your position in the list.

design_principles.name: Affordances must be real
design_principles.why: A visible shortcut or control that does nothing is worse than none: it teaches the user the interface is decorative.
design_principles.in_practice: Ship the behaviour or remove the hint. Keyboard affordances are shown only where the binding exists.

design_principles.name: Empty and error states are primary screens
design_principles.why: Day one is an empty pool, and the first failure is where trust is won or lost — yet these are usually the least-designed screens in a product.
design_principles.in_practice: Empty states name the next action. Errors distinguish 'the server is unreachable' from 'your filters matched nobody' and offer a retry, because showing an empty table for a network failure misleads the recruiter.

design_principles.name: Ask at activation, not at the door
design_principles.why: Setup questions asked before the user has seen value are unanswerable and expensive; the same question after value is obvious and cheap.
design_principles.in_practice: Land users in a working, populated app. Collect company and team details at the moment they are first needed — first publish, first invite.

typography.rationale: Type carries the identity so colour does not have to. The editorial serif is reserved for the report at /report, which is a persuasion artifact for a different audience; it has no business on a candidate row.
rules: Numbers a user compares across rows are tabular-nums, always.
Monospace is reserved for machine-produced values, labels and keys — never for prose.
Labels are wayfinding: minimum 11px and at least 70% contrast against their background. Small and faint at once is not allowed.

color_palette.note: Values below are the current dark surface. Colour is assigned by role, not by brand. A light-first surface is planned; when it lands these token names stay and only their values change, so no component needs editing.
color_palette.forbidden: Do not introduce a decorative accent that carries no state meaning.

buttons.primary: .btn .btn-primary — exactly one per screen, the action we want taken
buttons.rule: A button's visual weight must match how often it is the right choice.

components.score: Never a bare figure. Always: bar + number + a control that reveals the breakdown.
components.cards: bg-surface, 1px #262626 border, generous internal padding, square-ish corners.
components.tables: Dense rows, hairline separators, hover and keyboard cursor states distinguishable from each other.

motion.rule: Motion may explain a state change or show progress. It may not perform.
motion.in_practice: Snappy colour transitions on hover. No scale or translate on dashboard elements — perceived speed is a feature for someone doing this eight hours a day. Scanning/progress animations are permitted only where real latency exists.

mock_data_requirements.context: Indian names, companies and salary ranges. Professional, no stereotypes.
mock_data_requirements.rule: Mock data must include awkward cases — missing notice period, unstated education, near-miss candidates — because those are what the design has to survive.

testing_attributes.rules: All interactive elements MUST carry data-testid attributes. Example: data-testid='cand-score-<id>'.
